correctness.rationale: Induction gives Z_n[i]=1+nu_2(i). A rank-k<n center has equal flanks out to distance 2^(k-1)-1; at the next distance the consecutive multiples of 2^k have unequal ranks, or the wrapped endpoint has rank 1 and its interior counterpart higher rank. All allowed strings at a given rank and radius agree. The sole rank-n center and the only equal-adjacent pair (at the seam, modulo the period) are global reflection centers. Thus the count applies even to lengths beyond a period. Consecutive occurrences at rank k<n are centered 2^k apart, except for one wrap gap of 2^k-1. In the regular case the return is centered at a higher-rank midpoint and fits its equal flanks; in the seam case the midpoint is a global reflection center. Returns between successive rank-n centers or successive seams are centered at the other reflection type. This remains valid with overlapping occurrences of long palindromes. The complete-return criterion gives richness and hence coincidence of privileged and palindrome factor sets. At n=1 the constant word has one factor of each length, and each is privileged by its return to the preceding length (length one being initial). Summing the odd contributions through one circumference gives N and the even ones give (N-1)/2, including the N=1 boundary.
residual_risks: The finite code checks only its stated ranks and lengths; the exact all-length result instead follows from the reflection and return proof.

evidence: Every length-at-most-N circular factor is a factor of Z_n squared, so the square contains the known (3N-1)/2 nonempty palindromes at those lengths.
The middle seam of the square joins two identical palindromic blocks. For each even length strictly above N through 2N it supplies one distinct longer palindrome, adding (N+1)/2.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The square has at least 2N nonempty palindromes, meeting the general length bound. It is rich, so the periodic word is rich by Theorem 3.1 and privileged complexity equals palindromic complexity, also on the perimeter. For odd length above N, a centered length-N subpalindrome must be the unique one, Z_n, whose rank-n center occurs once per period. For even length a center must be the unique equal-letter seam modulo N (n=1 is trivial). Both centers extend by global reflection, so there is exactly one palindrome of each longer length. This gives the complete remainder by direct implication without needing a new return classification.
